findings.explanation: kube-state-metrics names these families kube_rolebinding_* and kube_clusterrolebinding_* (for example kube_rolebinding_info with roleref_kind and roleref_name labels), and they are only emitted when the rolebindings/clusterrolebindings resources are enabled. Searching for kube_role_binding never matches.
findings.quote: kube-state-metrics families kube_role_binding and kube_clusterrole_binding for RBAC inventory corroboration
findings.suggested_fix: Use kube_rolebinding_info and kube_clusterrolebinding_info, note that they are EXPERIMENTAL and must be enabled with --resources=rolebindings,clusterrolebindings, and mention that roleref_name lets you inventory cluster-admin bindings directly.

findings.explanation: In an audit PolicyRule, an empty namespaces list matches every namespace and the empty string "" is required to match cluster-scoped resources; wildcards are not documented for this field. With namespaces: ["*"], ClusterRoleBinding and ClusterRole requests (cluster-scoped) do not match the RequestResponse rule, so the cluster-admin bindings this UC is built to catch lose their requestObject.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the namespaces lines from the sample policy (empty list = all namespaces and cluster-scoped), or list "" explicitly for cluster-scoped resources.

findings.explanation: The stanza timestamp parser defaults to layout_type strptime, so a Go reference-time layout fails to parse unless layout_type: gotime is set; the repository guide uses a strptime layout for the same receiver.
findings.suggested_fix: Add layout_type: gotime under timestamp, or use the strptime layout shown in docs/guides/kubernetes.md.

findings.explanation: The SPL only inspects rolebindings and clusterrolebindings (and only roleRef name cluster-admin); Role/ClusterRole mutations and wildcard verbs or resources in rules are never evaluated, yet the title promises excessive-permission detection and Troubleshooting Case 2 describes wildcard ClusterRole updates as if the search raised them.
findings.quote: who can mutate Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding, and ClusterRole objects, who receives cluster-admin or wildcard-equivalent grants
findings.suggested_fix: Either state plainly that excessive permissions are detected only via cluster-admin bindings, or describe the additional roles/clusterroles arm (rules containing "*" verbs, resources or escalate/bind/impersonate verbs) the reader must add. Also fix the typo 'ClusterRole objects' to 'ClusterRoleBinding objects'.

findings.explanation: With a 24-hour window and no deduplication, every qualifying event is re-reported on each of the 96 daily runs, and the 45-minute throttle described in Step 3 cannot stop that; latest=@h also delays detection of a cluster-admin grant by up to an hour. The savedsearches.conf sketch sets dispatch.latest_time = now, which the inline latest=@h overrides.
findings.quote: Save uc_3_2_12_rbac_anomalies on a fifteen-minute cadence over earliest=-24h@h latest=@h
findings.suggested_fix: Alert on a short rolling window (for example earliest=-20m latest=-5m on a 15-minute schedule) and keep the 24-hour window only for the signal_volume_24h context via a separate summary or dashboard search.

findings.explanation: Generator checklist residue aimed at the authoring pipeline, not the implementer (also 'Fenced SPL for runbooks must match the spl JSON field byte-for-byte').
findings.quote: Closing checklist: five em-dash step headers present; Step 3 fenced SPL matches spl; multisearch lists five arms including kube-state-metrics scrape; coalesce appears in each audit arm
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the closing checklist and the byte-for-byte note.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by a generic handle, but the SPL fails to parse and the metric names do not exist, so it cannot have been run.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/community until the search has been executed against real audit data.

findings.explanation: The URL is the generic access-control index, not the auditing page. The BSI link is also a generic landing page with no Kubernetes content.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug/debug-cluster/audit/ (as in the repository guide) and drop or replace the BSI landing-page link.

findings.explanation: The link text labels the OTel Helm chart as a 'Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes'; the repository guide names only the splunk-otel-collector Helm chart. The linked add-on page may not exist or may describe a different product.
findings.quote: Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes ([Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes](https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/AddOns/released/Kubernetes/About))
findings.suggested_fix: Link the Helm chart (https://github.com/signalfx/splunk-otel-collector-chart) and confirm whether a separately named Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes is actually required for field extractions.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The fifth multisearch arm contains stats dc(_raw) ... BY cluster _time; multisearch subsearches may contain only streaming commands, so the whole search fails with a multisearch error. Move the kube-state-metrics arm to an append or compute it after the multisearch.

The metrics arm filters on match(_raw, "kube_clusterrole_binding") OR match(_raw, "kube_role_binding"), which never matches the real kube-state-metrics names kube_clusterrolebinding_* / kube_rolebinding_*.

The prod exec arm keeps only resp_code 200-299, but streaming exec/attach/portforward requests are upgraded connections whose audit responseStatus.code is commonly 101 Switching Protocols, so successful production exec may never be reported. Verify the logged code on a test cluster and accept 101.

Missing responseStatus.code defaults to "201" (treated as success) in three arms, and the trusted_admin_users join with max=0 duplicates rows when a user has several cluster rows; the Authentication tstats join rarely matches Kubernetes usernames.

The cimSpl counts Authentication events per user and action without any RBAC filter, so it does not express this detection; RBAC binding mutations map to the Change data model (All_Changes with object_category / object and action created/modified), which the repository guide lists for kube:apiserver:audit create/update/patch.
T1098 could be narrowed to T1098.006 (Additional Container Cluster Roles), and the production exec lane maps to T1609 (Container Administration Command).

summary: Strong threat framing and useful validation and troubleshooting cases, but the SPL will not run (stats inside multisearch), the kube-state-metrics metric names are wrong, the sample audit policy and OTel config would silently miss cluster-scoped bindings and fail timestamp parsing, and the 'excessive permission' half of the title (wildcard Roles and ClusterRoles) is never searched.
